text:
Alex: Quick FYI — hit a routing bug in staging/prod split. Mobile client sends `X-Cust-Env: staging` and the gateway honored it, routing to the staging pool even for prod tokens. Not ideal :grimacing:
Maya: Oof. Can you paste the route rule that matched?
Alex: Sure — here's the snippet from the envoy config that matched earlier:
```yaml
- match:
    headers:
      - name: X-Cust-Env
        exact: staging
  route: pool-staging
```
Alex: We also have an old rule that prefers `X-Client-UA` for canary routing, which is probably related.
Julian: We shouldn't trust client-supplied headers for routing decisions. Always use auth-proxy-populated headers or JWT claims. Client headers are trivially spoofable. :warning:
Nina: We do need UA for telemetry, but that should be separate from routing. UA normalization and a separate telemetry header injected by the edge would be better.
Samir: Also note quotas are keyed off org id in the auth token. If routing or tier decisions rely on client headers, quotas could be circumvented. We should treat any header from the public internet as untrusted unless the auth-proxy or internal network overwrote it.
Maya: Agreed. Proposed fix: strip `X-Cust-Env` and `X-Client-UA` at the edge unless the request originates from our internal IPs or has `x-rdwd-auth-ctx` present. Then use `x-rdwd-tenant` (injected by auth-proxy) for routing and `x-rdwd-client-ua` for telemetry.
Alex: That sounds right. Minimal config change I can test locally: add header removal filter + prefer `x-rdwd-tenant` header in route match.
Maya: Example change I'm going to prepare for the gateway (Envoy-style):
```yaml
- name: envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.header_to_metadata.v3.Config
    request_rules:
      - header: "x-rdwd-tenant"
        on_header_present: { metadata_namespace: "auth", key: "tenant" }
- name: envoy.filters.http.lua
  typed_config: # small lua to drop untrusted headers from public traffic
    inline_code: |
      function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
        local src = request_handle:headers():get("x-forwarded-for") or ""
        if not src:match("10\\.") then -- naive internal check
          request_handle:headers():remove("x-cust-env")
          request_handle:headers():remove("x-client-ua")
        end
      end
```
Julian: Minor nit: don't rely on a naive IP check in prod. Use the trusted network list in infra or the `via`/`x-envoy-internal` flag. I'll add a rule to the infra config to mark internal requests.
Nina: I'll add a UA normalization lambda in telemetry so we don't have 40 different browser strings. Also will wire `x-rdwd-client-ua` into our dashboards.
Samir: I'll run an audit on quota enforcement and make sure quota keys come from JWT claims only. If anyone's relying on `X-Cust-Env` for billing/quotas, we need to stop that now.
Alex: I'll open a PR with the header-strip and route preference patch. Will canary to `eng-platform-canary` first.
Maya: Thanks — please link the PR here. Also create a small migration note for support; we might see some weird routing for old clients.
deploy-bot: Deployment started: gateway/2026-03-18T15:12:30Z to canary cluster :rocket:
Alex: PR is up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7892 — includes tests and an integration config for the canary.
Julian: Reviewing now. If all green, let's ship the header-strip with a 1% canary for 6 hours.
Nina: Will update dashboards to reflect new header `x-rdwd-client-ua` mapping.
Samir: I'll follow up with a quota audit ticket and tag infra/security.
Alex: Thanks all. Outcome: stop trusting public headers for routing, prefer auth-proxy injected headers, strip client headers at edge, add UA normalization, and audit quotas. :thumbsup:
